newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish finance min sees '97 growth down to 6 pct.
newsitem.headline: Polish finance min sees '97 growth down to 6 pct.

text.p: Polish finance minister Grzegorz Kolodko said he expected growth to slow to about 6.0 percent in 1997 from an estimated 6.6 percent in 1996.

"I believe that the 1996 growth was 6.6 percent rather that six percent (as estimated by the Central Statistical Office)," Kolodko said in an interview for Reuter Financial Television, taped over the weekend at the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland and aired on Monday.
"This year, I expect to have no less than six percent (growth)," he added.
He said investment was likely to be the main engine of growth this year. Last year, domestic consumption and investment replaced exports as the main contributors to growth.
Kolodko also said Poland was unlikely to have a balanced budget in the near future, partly bacause planned social security reforms will require a temporary rise in subsidies from the central budget.
The higher subsidies will help spin off new privately-managed pensions funds, which will gradually take part of the social security burden.
Once the funds become opearational, subsidies to the social security system will start to fall, Kolodko said. -- Warsaw Newsroom +48 22 653 9700
